    • canRetryWithin

      public static boolean canRetryWithin(@Nullable ApiHttpHeaders headers, int statusCode, long maxDelayMillis)
      Whether a rate-limited response can usefully be retried within the configured maximum delay.

      A rate limit window is a hard boundary: until it resets, every request is rejected. So if the server asks for longer than we are willing to wait, capping the delay does not salvage the retry — it guarantees the next attempt lands inside the same window and fails again, and the one after that, until the budget is gone. The caller ends up waiting maxRetries * maxDelay and still gets the error, having added load to a server that was already shedding it.

      Failing immediately is more useful: the caller gets the 429 straight away and can decide what to do with it, rather than being blocked on attempts that cannot succeed.

      This applies to 429 only. A Retry-After on a 503 is the server's estimate of when it might recover, not a hard boundary, so an early retry there may well succeed and the delay is capped rather than abandoned.

      Returns:
      false when there is no timing header at all, or when the wait it asks for exceeds maxDelayMillis
